Theorem
[Fredholm alternative]1. ch5:5.3\group chapter-5 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0088, page-0089, page-0090

↗ gt.def5.3.compact-mapping ↗ gt.lem5.4 Let $T:\V \to \V $ be compact and linear. Exactly one of the following holds:

  1. $x-Tx=0$ has a nonzero solution;

  2. for every $y\in \V $, the equation $x-Tx=y$ has a unique solution, and $(I-T)^{-1}$ is bounded.
